title: Tenant Penalty Ledger and Timebound SLO Rescuer
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Motivation: We observed repeated regional slowpaths where tenants with short, bursty workloads repeatedly triggered SLO enforcement and then recovered, causing oscillation and noisy eviction churn. This PR introduces a Tenant Penalty Ledger (TPL) and a Timebound SLO Rescuer that together smooth enforcement decisions and provide a safe rollback path for aggressive egress/eviction policies. Scope: - Introduce an append-only in-memory penalty ledger per-tenant (sharded) that tracks recent SLO infractions (latency or error budget breaches) as decayed tokens. - Make enforcement decisions consult the TPL and only escalate eviction/throttle when a tenant exceeds a timebound penalty threshold (configurable window + decay rate). - Add a Rescue mode that can be triggered automatically if the cluster sees >3% eviction churn in a 5-minute window: Rescue mode relaxes aggressive egress caps and enables a fast rollback route through the new egress-proxy guard. - Add telemetry hooks and a compact audit log for every enforcement decision (ledger read/write, decision reason, last-eviction-id). - Backwards-safe hotfix wrapper: config flags default to off; rollout via feature flag and a canary master rollout plan documented in the PR. Checklist: - [x] Implementation (runtime + control plane adapters) - [x] Unit tests for penalty decay, ledger sharding, and decision gating - [x] Integration test covering eviction -> rescue -> rollback cycle - [x] Telemetry dashboards + alert rule updates - [x] Docs (runtime config + ops runbook) Key behaviors and safeguards: - Ledger is bounded (max 512 tokens per tenant) and uses exponential decay to avoid permanent punishment for short spikes. - Timebound threshold is tenant-configurable; default 10 tokens in 15 minutes (safe conservative). - Rescue mode requires a 2/3 sampling confirmation from regional health probes before soft-relaxing egress caps. - Egress-proxy rollback is idempotent and annotated in audit logs for traceability. Why this is different: existing SLO guards act on instantaneous metrics or rolling averages only; the TPL exposes a short-term memory that prevents flip-flop between enforcement and reinstatement, and Rescue mode provides an automated stability backstop to prevent cluster-wide oscillation. Rollout plan: 1) Feature flag behind rollout gate (ops-only). 2) Canary in us-west-2 small region for 24h with verbose telemetry. 3) Gradual ramp to additional regions over 72h, monitoring eviction churn, latency p99, and failed request percentage. Related: ENG-1345 describes the oscillation incident that motivated the ledger; ENG-1372 captures the operator runbook asks.

review_comments: Ethan Morales (2026-02-12): Nice approach. Two asks: 1) make decay window configurable per-tenant (default ok), 2) add a hard upper bound on ledger memory usage. Please add a unit test covering ledger overflow behavior.

Priya Kapoor (2026-02-12): Responding: decay window is tenant-configurable via config/api.yaml; ledger is bounded to 512 tokens and we added eviction LRU fallback. Added unit test for overflow in commits e91f3b0 and 2b3c4d5.
Sofia Lind (2026-02-14): Telemetry looks good, but the Rescue mode requires clearer guard rails. Can we add a sampling confirmation from regional probes?
Priya Kapoor (2026-02-14): Added probe confirmation (2/3) and made rescue window configurable. Updated docs with probe rationale.
Arjun Patel (2026-02-16): Integration test flaked once on CI (timing). Recommend using deterministic clock in tests.
Priya Kapoor (2026-02-16): Switched to test clock and reran e2e; CI green on rerun.
release_notes: Adds Tenant Penalty Ledger (short-term tokenized infractions) and a Timebound SLO Rescue mode that prevents eviction oscillation. Feature is behind a feature flag and off by default. Ops: follow docs/ops/penalty-ledger-runbook.md for canary and rollback steps.
